title: Refactor metering pipeline to attribute cache and batch costs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Recent incidents and quota reconciliation reports show inconsistent billing when requests hit prefix/KV caches and when multiple customer requests are coalesced into a single GPU batch. Two concrete failure modes were observed: (1) cache-prefetched responses were receiving 0 compute charge but still consumed per-request quota tokens incorrectly in quota dashboards; (2) coalesced batches that reused KV cache or prefetching were being counted multiple times across the aggregated requests, causing customers to be billed for duplicated token compute. This ticket refactors the metering pipeline to calculate an authoritative per-request billing attribution before and after batch coalescing and to preserve correct quota/rate-limit semantics for cached responses.
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative per-request token cost is recorded in metering events for every request, including cache hits, and matches the new cost model
Coalesced batch billing charges each customer only for their attributable compute tokens (no double-counting)
Rate limiting and quota enforcement reflect request-level semantics: cache-hit requests can consume request-rate quota but only charge compute if applicable and per the policy
Backfill reconciliation job can detect and correct historical overcharges within a configurable window and emit a report
Integration tests cover at least: pure cache-hit, mixed cache-hit + compute, fully coalesced multi-tenant batch with partial cache reuse, and staggered prefetch aggregation
proposed_solution: Introduce a two-stage metering model: (A) Request Attribution Phase — compute a lightweight per-request 'attribution record' capturing: request_id, customer_id, model_variant, requested_seq_len, prefix_cache_hit (bool), kv_cache_hit_ratio (float), estimated_prefetch_tokens; (B) Batch Aggregation Phase — when requests are coalesced, compute batch-level compute tokens once, then allocate billable compute tokens back to requests using deterministic allocation rules

Allocation rules: cached tokens (prefix/KV hit) are assigned zero compute cost; shared compute work in a coalesced batch is allocated proportionally by 'marginal token delta' (the additional tokens the request forced the batch to generate) with a minimum per-request floor of 1 token for bookkeeping

Treat prefetch/pipeline fills specially: tokens used solely for prefetch that are later consumed by subsequent requests are tagged as 'prefetch_shared' and charged to the original request owner or to a configurable tenant-level prefetch bucket depending on product settings
Add an immutable event tag 'metering_unified_version' to all recorded events so we can detect mixed-state writes and run a backfill to reconcile prior inconsistent meters

Update rate limiter to consume both 'request tokens' and 'compute tokens' separately, where request tokens decrement an RPS quota and compute tokens decrement usage quotas; cache-hit requests may still consume request tokens while compute tokens equal zero
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy attribution-only changes to canary region (us-west-2) for 7 days; emit parallel metering events (old and new) to compare delta metrics without impacting billing, alert on >0.5% divergence
Phase 2 (pilot): enable unified metering for 5 mid-market customers selected with accounting team; collect reconciliation reports and customer feedback for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (global): switch billing pipeline to authoritative new metering and run reconciliation backfill for past 30 days; issue customer notifications and credit refunds where needed
Fallback: if unexpected >1% revenue discrepancy or critical quota regressions are observed, rollback batch allocation component and retire new attribution until fixes applied
testing_notes: Unit tests for allocation algorithm covering edge cases: single-request batch, identical seq_len multi-tenant batch, large outlier seq_len dominating batch cost
E2E tests in staging with synthetic workload generator that simulates KV cache hit ratios and prefetch behavior; assert metering event counts and sum of allocated tokens == batch_compute_tokens
Load test: ensure new allocation computation adds <5% CPU overhead to serving path at P99 load, otherwise move to async attribution consumer
Create QA dashboard showing per-request attributed tokens, batch tokens, and historical diffs versus old meter for the canary window
notes: Design review 2025-11-10: agreed on two-stage model and proportional allocation with a floor to avoid zero-allocation bookkeeping issues (attendees: Ravi Menon, Sofia Martinez, Aisha Patel)
Accounting input: prefer conservative customer refunds; billing team requested a 30-day backfill window and manual approval step for mass credits
OSS concern: SDKs that surface token counts must be version-gated; plan to add 'metering_unified_version' to SDK responses in next minor release
Related infra work: storage schema change for metering_events table to include attribution fields (planned ENG-16500 schema-migration)
